newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C.Bank sees volatile peso in first few days.
newsitem.headline: Manila C.Bank sees volatile peso in first few days.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Friday he expected the peso to be very volatile in the first few days after the currency was effectively devalued.
"We expect that (the peso) in the first few days to be very volatile ... while the peso is seeking its own level," Sinsgon told reporters at a news conference.
The Central Bank said early on Friday that it was allowing the peso to move within a wider range. It did not specify a range and said the market would find the right balance for the peso-dollar rate.

Asked if the peso's 11 percent fall on Friday would affect the economy, Singson said: "We expect a slight uptick in inflation. I'm sure it will be tolerable. I am very confident that it will not be double digit."
Singson said he had not yet sought the assistance of other central banks in South East Asia.
But the Philippines had been assured of help by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), he said.
"IMF has assured us of financial assistance," he said, adding that the Philippines still had an undrawn balance of SDRs equal to $1.05 billion.

Asked why the Central Bank had changed its earlier policy under which it used intervention as well as interest rates to strongly defend the peso, Singson said: "The speculators were no longer responding to overnight rate ... we don't like to dissipate our precious reserves."
